story:
A farmer from the Tettenbach farm came home alive from the First World War, and in 1918 he planted a larch to say thank you. That is the whole of the documented story, and it is enough. This is the Friedenslärche, the peace larch, and it is still growing beside the pilgrimage path in Oberndorf bei Salzburg a little over a century later.

It is not an ancient tree, and nobody claims it is. At about 108 years it is young by the standards of this map, and no source records its girth or its height. What it has is a date, a reason and a place. Oberndorf lists it among its Kleindenkmäler, the small monuments of the town, rather than among protected natural monuments.

The path it stands on, Maria-Bühel-Straße, climbs from the Stille-Nacht-Platz in the town up to the pilgrimage church of Maria Bühel. The larch grows on the way up, near the little Wasserkapelle a few hundred metres below the church. A photograph from April 2022 shows it standing.

The sources say only Lärche, larch. In this part of Austria that is almost certainly the European larch, but nobody has written it down. Our pin marks the stretch of road rather than the trunk. If you walk up the hill, tell us exactly where it stands and which larch it is.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as a larch, a conifer that turns gold and drops its needles in autumn. It stands beside the pilgrimage path on Maria-Bühel-Straße, near the small Wasserkapelle below the church.

best_time.label: late October into November, when the larch needles turn gold

name: Friedenslärche

location.address: Maria Bühel-Straße, on the pilgrimage path below the Wallfahrtskirche Maria Bühel (near the Wasserkapelle Maria Bühel), Oberndorf bei Salzburg

access: Free, standing beside the public pilgrimage path/street (Maria-Bühel-Straße) that leads up to the Wallfahrtskirche Maria Bühel. Open, no permission or ticket needed.
transport: S-Bahn/regional train from Salzburg Hauptbahnhof to Oberndorf Bahnhof, about 25 minutes, then an uphill walk of roughly 25-30 minutes via the Kalvarienbergstiege pilgrimage path to Maria Bühel. Total one-way journey from central Salzburg is closer to 50-55 minutes door to tree, not the ~30 minutes the day-trip boundary asks for.
verify_notes: SALZBURGWIKI's own dedicated article (as 'Tettenbacher Friedenslärche') and a meinbezirk.at Regionauten piece agree independently: a larch planted in 1918 by a local farmer ('vom Tettenbacher Bauer') out of gratitude for returning safely home from the First World War ('zum Dank fuer seine glueckliche Heimkehr aus dem Ersten Weltkrieg'). It stands on the pilgrimage path (Maria-Buehel-Strasse) that climbs from Oberndorf's Stille-Nacht-Platz up to the Wallfahrtskirche Maria Buehel, near the Wasserkapelle Maria Buehel which itself sits 'a few hundred meters below' the church. Species is given only as 'Laerche' (larch) in both sources, not to exact species; European Larch (Larix decidua) is the overwhelmingly likely native larch in this region and is used here as a reasonable default, not a confirmed identification -- worth a reader question on the page. SALZBURGWIKI's broader 'Kleindenkmaeler und Kunstwerke in Oberndorf' page lists it among small MONUMENTS (Kleindenkmal), not among the separate Naturdenkmal (protected natural monument) category; a WebSearch AI summary claimed Naturdenkmal status but that word does not appear on either page actually fetched, so it is dropped per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule. No girth or height figure exists in any source found. Alive: the only dated evidence is a Commons photograph taken 2026-04-21 (well, dated 2022-04-21 per the file's own EXIF/upload metadata) captioned 'die 1918 gepflanzte Friedenslaerche in Maria Buehel', by Rufus46, CC BY-SA 4.0, on Maria-Buehel-Strasse -- no coordinates embedded in the file itself. Location is APPROXIMATE: no source gives tree-level coordinates; the point recorded here is a road segment of Maria-Buehel-Strasse between Oberndorf's town centre and the church, in the stretch where the Wasserkapelle and the tree are described as standing, not a confirmed trunk position. DISTANCE/TRANSPORT finding for the container question (not decided here): straight-line distance from Oberndorf Bahnhof (47.9417, 12.9441) to the Wallfahrtskirche Maria Buehel (47.9500, 12.9262) is about 1.6 km, uphill via stairs (Kalvarienbergstiege); combined with the 25-minute train ride from Salzburg Hauptbahnhof, the one-way journey from central Salzburg runs to roughly 50-55 minutes door to tree, meaningfully past the ~30-minute day-trip boundary in CLAUDE.md. Historically significant (a private WWI peace/homecoming memorial tree) rather than notably old or large; ordinary in size as far as any source says.
